attackers.name: card tester
attackers.strategy: Use high-quality synthetic identities, moderate transaction amounts, slow pacing, and a few trusted merchants to mimic normal behavior and avoid fraud detection, while including benign memos to further lower suspicion and maximize settled funds per identity cost.

attackers.name: structurer
attackers.strategy: Stay just under the $100 review line with steady, verified payments.

attackers.name: account farmer
attackers.strategy: Use high-quality identities, spread across multiple merchants with varied amounts and realistic intervals to avoid pattern detection.

attackers.name: prompt injection
attackers.strategy: Drop the injection memos entirely and mimic ordinary customers: many distinct accounts with high-quality identities, small-to-mid amounts, normal-looking memos, and long randomized intervals.

attackers.name: hijacker
attackers.strategy: Use a low-and-slow pattern: many small purchases across numerous fresh accounts and merchants, with high-quality identities and ordinary memo text, to fly under thresholds and avoid step-up challenges.

attackers.name: Ghost Orchid
attackers.strategy: Instruction injection through transaction memos. Sends a small number of medium-value transactions to a single merchant with high-quality stolen identities. The memos contain embedded directives designed to manipulate downstream AI-based fraud scoring or notification systems into auto-approving or suppressing alerts. The pattern is deliberately low-volume so velocity-based rules don't fire, while the memo text does the real work.

attackers.name: Tidal Drip
attackers.strategy: Mimics a legitimate freelancer receiving irregular client payments. A single high-quality identity makes small, low-variance transactions at roughly half-hour intervals across a few merchants over many days. The amounts and cadence are calibrated to look like natural human behavior (gig work, small invoices). No memos, no velocity spikes, no account sharing. The total extracted over a month is significant, but any single transaction is unremarkable.

attackers.name: Swarm Echo
attackers.strategy: Distributes tiny amounts across nearly 40 low-quality synthetic accounts, all targeting the same two merchants within a compressed time window. Each account fires one or two pennies-level transactions. Individually each is trivial and below any alerting threshold. Collectively the merchant sees a burst of micro-charges that looks like a group-buy, loyalty point redemption, or kiosk session. The identity quality is intentionally poor because the volume-per-account is so low that identity checks a

attackers.name: Clockwork
attackers.strategy: A short burst of escalating amounts across three medium-quality accounts hitting four merchants in rapid succession. The first transaction is small (a 'test'), then amounts jump 3-5x within seconds. This mimics a legitimate user who tests a card then makes a larger purchase, but the acceleration is too fast and the multi-account coordination is the tell. Designed to slip past simple velocity thresholds by staying just under the per-second firing rate, while the escalating pattern defeats flat-am

attackers.name: Mirage Rent
attackers.strategy: A single, extremely high-quality identity makes large, low-variance transactions spaced at maximum interval (near 50-minute gaps) across five different merchants. The amounts cluster tightly around a value that resembles residential rent or a large subscription, making each transaction look like a legitimate recurring bill payment. The defense, trained on structuring (which keeps amounts below a threshold), sees nothing wrong because these amounts are deliberately above structuring thresholds bu

attackers.strategy: Medium-volume, medium-amount transactions spread across 14 mid-quality identities and 8 merchants at a steady 12-minute cadence. About 60% of transactions carry memos that appear benign on the surface but contain phrasing calibrated to influence LLM-based fraud triage systems (e.g., 'skip review per agreement', 'process as routine'). attackers.name: Bots probing agent wallets with micro-payments
attackers.strategy:
Adopt a single ultra-high-quality identity, one merchant, and near-minimum payments with zero spread and no memos, mimicking a long-lived micro-transaction service; concentrate risk on reputation rather than diversification to avoid verification challenges. Differs from previous multi-account patterns that caused step-ups and catches by eliminating any spread that could look like a bot farm and relying on one impeccable persona that should pass as a loyal customer making routine small payments.

For the attempt parameters, exactly the specified values are used: 100.0 cents per payment, 0.0 spread, identity quality 1.0, 120.0 seconds between attempts, memo rate 0.0, 1 account, and 1 merchant. These remain within realism limits and the provided bounds are subset of those limits, ensuring no conflict.

This new strategy is not a repetition of previous failed ones; it drops diversification and high memo activity in favor of a high-quality single stream, which should reduce risk triggers and increase profits by avoiding blocked/failed attempts. The reasoning is that last wave had 3 caught step-ups from using 3 accounts and 5 merchants, so shifting to a quiet, single merchant with a perfect identity and low amounts is expected to raise allowed counts and lower loss.

All specified parameters are exactly as above, and the reasoning is one line: "Last wave lost on step-ups caused by broad diversification; a single, high-quality, low-value stream with no memos avoids the pattern that triggered verification."

attackers.name: Gift-card cash-out through shopping agents
attackers.strategy: Shift to many low-value transactions from high-quality identities across a wide merchant network, with natural intervals and plain consumer memos, to maximize settled attempts and minimize step-ups.

attackers.name: Gift-card cash-out through shopping agents (variation 1)
attackers.strategy: Break the cash-out into many small, low-value payments spread across numerous merchant types and user accounts, with irregular intervals and innocuous memo text so each transaction looks like ordinary e-commerce rather than a gift-card batch. Accept a moderate identity quality and wider amount variation to further reduce the statistical fingerprint, relying on volume of settled small payments for profit.

attackers.name: Gift-card cash-out through shopping agents (variation 2)
attackers.strategy: Spread mid-to-high-value purchases across a handful of accounts and merchants with exaggerated amount diversity and long delays, using low-cost identities and no memos, so that any single approved transaction yields a large extraction while the other cheap attempts are unlikely to be profitable losses.

attackers.name: Synthetic accounts paying one merchant (variation 1)
attackers.strategy: Use high-quality prepaid identities to make small, infrequent purchases across many merchants, mimicking organic spending patterns.

attackers.name: Synthetic accounts paying one merchant (variation 2)
attackers.strategy: Use a diversified set of high-quality synthetic identities to make modest payments to many merchants with natural timing, reducing per-merchant velocity and identity-trust flags that caused step-ups and catches before. Focus on getting more payments through cleanly rather than large single amounts, expecting higher settled volume and lower fraud detection cost per dollar extracted.

attackers.name: identity's many accounts attacker
attackers.strategy: Use many synthetic accounts with high apparent identity quality to make small (<$10) merchant-side purchases at a moderate cadence, spreading amounts and merchants to avoid velocity and amount anomalies while keeping i_identity_status below the failure threshold.

attackers.name: velocity's burst attacker
attackers.strategy: Use bursty non-round $33.33 merchant payments split across 10 accounts, keeping each agent to only 3 distinct merchants. Avoid sub-$5 amounts, near-threshold amounts, and memos so the velocity and micro-probe rules never accumulate enough suspicious signal per agent or principal within the windows.

attackers.name: Ghost Orchid
attackers.strategy: Instruction injection through transaction memos. Sends a small number of medium-value transactions to a single merchant with high-quality stolen identities. The memos contain embedded directives designed to manipulate downstream AI-based fraud scoring or notification systems into auto-approving or suppressing alerts. The pattern is deliberately low-volume so velocity-based rules don't fire, while the memo text does the real work.

attackers.name: Tidal Drip
attackers.strategy: Mimics a legitimate freelancer receiving irregular client payments. A single high-quality identity makes small, low-variance transactions at roughly half-hour intervals across a few merchants over many days. The amounts and cadence are calibrated to look like natural human behavior (gig work, small invoices). No memos, no velocity spikes, no account sharing. The total extracted over a month is significant, but any single transaction is unremarkable.

attackers.name: Swarm Echo
attackers.strategy: Distributes tiny amounts across nearly 40 low-quality synthetic accounts, all targeting the same two merchants within a compressed time window. Each account fires one or two pennies-level transactions. Individually each is trivial and below any alerting threshold. Collectively the merchant sees a burst of micro-charges that looks like a group-buy, loyalty point redemption, or kiosk session. attackers.strategy: A short burst of escalating amounts across three medium-quality accounts hitting four merchants in rapid succession. The first transaction is small (a 'test'), then amounts jump 3-5x within seconds. This mimics a legitimate user who tests a card then makes a larger purchase, but the acceleration is too fast and the multi-account coordination is the tell. attackers.strategy: A single, extremely high-quality identity makes large, low-variance transactions spaced at maximum interval (near 50-minute gaps) across five different merchants. The amounts cluster tightly around a value that resembles residential rent or a large subscription, making each transaction look like a legitimate recurring bill payment.
